Thanks to GTA 6 Foundation, Rockstar Promises Next Game Won't Take as Long to Release
articles.chapeau: Rockstar says their next game won't take eight years to be released, thanks to shared knowledge and tech from GTA 6.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 might be the most anticipated video game of all time, and part of the allure is how long gamers have waited for a sequel to GTA 5, a game that spanned two console generations and was initially released 13 years ago.
While gamers have waited more than a decade for a proper follow-up, Rockstar Games did release another title in between, and it’s none other than the highly acclaimed Red Dead Redemption 2, which was released in 2018.
Even if you factor Red Dead 2’s release, that’s still eight years between releases, which translates to one new game per console generation.
Thankfully, that might be the last time we’re going to wait this long for a Rockstar game release.
In a new feature on the making of GTA 6 by Bloomberg , Rockstar Games Head of Development Phil Hooker and Aaron Garbut talked about the making of the sixth mainline entry in the best-selling franchise.
While GTA 6 took ages to make, the studio promises that thanks to the tech they’ve built and the team’s familiarity with one another, the devs promise their next project won’t take as long.
Part of the game’s “secret,” aside from its budget that seems unlimited, is the development team that’s been working together for decades. Garbut and Hooker mentioned that they’ve found success because they’ve been making games for many years and know how to get them released, stating, “The last 30 years has been practice for where we got to here. The team and us as individuals have been doing it for so long that there’s a sort of shared understanding, shared knowledge and a sort of shortcut to questions.”
Hooker chimes in as well, adding, “The engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly, I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content.”
Hooker concluded, “We foundationally changed a lot of stuff on this project,” Garbut says. “But now it’s done, and we’re not going to rip it apart.”
This is definitely good news. Mind, this isn’t confirmation that we’ll see GTA 7 released anytime soon, as Rockstar’s next project could very well be another Red Dead game — or something else entirely.
At the very least, gamers won’t have to wait 8-13 years for the next Rockstar Games opus to be conceived.
GTA 6 will be released on November 19 on the PS5 and PC, and a new rumor has surfaced stating that the PC version will be released in Q1 2027 .

GTA 6 Developer Rockstar Makes A Big Promise About Its Next Game
articles.chapeau: It took eight years for Rockstar to get Grand Theft Auto 6 ready to play, but it sounds like their next game won
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Some major news has dropped about the entire development process of "Grand Theft Auto 6," and it sheds some much-needed light on why it took so long to make. In a new exclusive feature from Bloomberg , reporter Jason Schreier went inside Rockstar North and spoke to a litany of developers and executives about "GTA 6," the company's past, and its future. While the main focus of the feature is the game's numerous delays and development timeline, there are also interesting tidbits about Rockstar's future beyond "GTA 6."
It's no secret that "GTA 6" underwent one of the longer development cycles for a game in recent memory. This was coupled with a couple of infamous delays that left the CEO of Take-Two Interactive, Strauss Zelnick, "flabbergasted." However, the entire strenuous development cycle for "GTA 6" has apparently armed Rockstar with the tools and knowledge needed to not let its next game take nearly as long to make.
Rockstar Games The three co-heads of development at Rockstar spoke with Bloomberg about the making of "GTA 6" and its delays. In short, Rockstar was forced to put all developers on "Red Dead Redemption 2" up until its release in 2018, and after that, "GTA 6" was left without a clear vision until roughly 2022. Finally, it took an immense amount of work to implement new systems and fulfill the ambitions for the game.
However, it all seemed to pay off in the long run, as Rockstar now feels that it's in a much better spot as a studio moving forward. Phil Hooker, one of the three heads of development at Rockstar, stated that future games will be far more streamlined as a result of "GTA 6," and it won't take another eight years to see a new release.
"The engine, the tools, and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly. I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content."
Fellow co-head of development Aaron Garbut echoed the same belief, saying, "We foundationally changed a lot of stuff on this project. But now it's done, and we're not going to rip it apart." From the sound of it, Rockstar seems to know what it needs to do to develop games faster and more efficiently. Of course, things won't return to the way they used to at Rockstar, which previously pumped out a new title nearly every year in the early 2000s. At the very least, though, it appears fans won't have to wait another decade to play Rockstar's next creation.
Rockstar Games While Rockstar told Bloomberg about how much it's learned from "GTA 6" and how it will affect its future development plans, there was nothing unveiled about the next game in the company's iconic library. It's widely assumed that a sequel to "Red Dead Redemption 2" would be next up on the docket, but there are currently no leaks or information surrounding that potential project.
Instead, Rockstar could develop the next iteration of one of its dormant franchises. It's been claimed that Rockstar has started and cancelled development of a "Bully" sequel on multiple occasions, so could the company return to the drawing board for that game? It seems unlikely but not out of the realm of possibility.
The far more likely franchise to get a reboot is "L.A. Noire," which has been recently rumored to be Rockstar's next project. According to old leaks on a "GTA" forum website , Rockstar has tossed around the idea of a "L.A. Noire" sequel in the past few years. While this rumor might not have much merit on its own, Rockstar acquired a game studio called Video Games Deluxe in 2025, which employs several of the original "L.A. Noire" developers. This company was renamed Rockstar Australia and has presumably been helping with "GTA 6" since it was acquired. However, perhaps now the studio will turn its attention to a new project that it has some past experience with.
Of course, with how tight-lipped Rockstar tends to be, we likely won't know about its next project for an extended period of time. Fortunately, though, it looks like players won't have to wait as long to play it thanks to "GTA 6" and its development.

articles.chapeau: Cyberleek promises not to reveal the ending of GTA 6, as long as Take-Two leaves them alone.
articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter It's a classic move: A villain, or sometimes a hero, inserts himself into a seemingly inescapable situation. Danger everywhere—no way out! But just as the good guys (or bad guys) are about to pounce, he holds up the pin he's pulled from the grenade under his coat, forcing everyone to back off! Escape is at hand!
That seems to be the strategy now adopted by notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek, and by "seems to be," I mean they stated it outright. In a message posted to their now-defunct website but preserved by GTA VI News on X , Cyberleek committed to not releasing anything more about GTA 6 —including its ending, which at this point remains unknown—as long as Take-Two lets everything slide.
"CL has the ending. It was considered," the message states. "It would punish Take-Two greatly—but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy—why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough.
"The ending stays unpublished. Proof: the latest leek—clips from the final missions, out of context, revealing nothing. The dead man's switch is active—story spoilers only. Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL chooses it."
A dead man's switch, generally speaking, is a switch built to be triggered if its operator is incapacitated. Miles Dyson, for instance, blew up Cyberdyne Systems with an improvised dead man's switch in Terminator 2 (not that it did much good) and Roger Murtaugh did the literal grenade-pin thing in Lethal Weapon while trying to save his daughter from Shadow Company goons. There are variants—in Point Break, for instance, Rosie was ordered to kill Johnny Utah's girlfriend if Bodhi didn't check in by 3, to ensure Johnny's participation in a bank robbery.
My own personal favorite dead man's switch comes from Hawk the Slayer:
That particular variation on the theme notwithstanding, dead man's switches are meant as last-ditch failsafes: If something bad happens to me, something much worse will happen to you .

It makes me wonder if Cyberleek's sudden withdrawal and proposed détente with Take-Two means that they're starting to feel the heat. Take-Two takes this sort of thing seriously as a matter of course, and you can bet it's going to go extra-hardass on anyone who messes with its biggest game ever, which GTA 6 unquestionably is. I have no doubt that life for Cyberleek will become very unpleasant, very quickly, if and when they're ever caught.
The problem Cyberleek faces, of course, is that their leverage—assuming it's real in the first place—has a very short shelf life. In six weeks at most, the GTA 6 ending will be out there, at which point there will be no shot left to shoot.
At best, then, this threat grants Cyberleek an extra month to find a deeper hole to hide in. And even that is wildly optimistic: Take-Two might be operating quietly, but I have no doubt that it's also operating furiously, and that there's not much of a mood to play 'I won't if you won't' games.
Cyberleek also defended their cryptocurrency ask, saying it "was always a donation, never an investment," and denying that a rugpull happened; they also said they wouldn't release the full build of GTA 6, with "full story mode, played to the end," because their memecoin market cap didn't hit $30 million .

articles.t: GTA 6 Reviews Will Be Released Before Launch
articles.chapeau: Insider Gaming has learned that Grand Theft Auto 6's reviews will be released ahead of the game's release. Get the full story here.
articles.txt:
Insider Gaming has learned that Grand Theft Auto 6’s review estate will go live before the release on November 19. This may come as a surprise to some, as plenty of gamers out there believed that GTA 6 would not have any reviews. It’s hardly the kind of game that needs to be reviewed, but the fact still stands that it will happen, and the content will drop before the game is in your hands (digitally).
While we have also learned the preliminary review embargo, we won’t be sharing that information as it’s subject to change in the run-up to the game being released.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game ever made. There’s no doubt about that. It’s set to be the fastest-selling game in history, and there are estimates that it might push to 50 million sales in one week . It will certainly eclipse Grand Theft Auto 5.
In recent weeks, we’ve seen much of Grand Theft Auto 6 pulled to pieces online as a dedicated leak campaign has revealed countless facts about the title. Additionally, some large-scale interviews, including those carried out in Rockstar North’s Edinburgh office , have divulged unparalleled amounts of information.
We know about as much as you could hope to know about Grand Theft Auto 6, and it still feels like we’re barely scratching the surface.
Most recently, it was claimed that GTA 6 would be arriving on PC platforms as early as Q1 2027, opening the game up to an entirely new and patient audience. It took a whopping nineteen months for GTA 5 to arrive on PC after launching on XBOX 360 and PlayStation 3 in 2013, so this rapid report is a turnaround for the books.
If you’re holding out for the reviews before you purchase Grand Theft Auto 6 (digitally), then you don’t have too long to wait. They’ll be going live before the game comes out, but as stated above, the exact embargo date is subject to change. They’re not here until they’re here.

articles.t: GTA 6 : après l'échec de sa cryptomonnaie, CyberLeek arrête les fuites, pour l'instant
articles.chapeau: Le jeton du leaker de GTA 6 n'a pas atteint les 30 millions de dollars visés. Il renonce au jeu complet, mais menace d'en révéler l'intrigue si on le fait…
articles.txt:
Le leaker anonyme qui diffuse depuis la mi-août des images d'une version de travail de GTA 6 vient d'annoncer la fin de sa campagne, sans publier le jeu complet. Dans un message en trois parties publié sur son site, que nous n'avons pas consulté, et rapporté par Kotaku, CyberLeek prend acte de l'échec de sa cryptomonnaie : « Les 30 millions n'ont pas été atteints, donc pas de version complète. »
Quand il menaçait de diffuser le jeu entier , CyberLeek promettait la version jouable si la capitalisation de sa monnaie atteignait 30 millions de dollars. Take-Two pouvait, selon lui, éviter la fuite en sortant GTA 6 sur disque et en présentant des excuses publiques. Kotaku situait cette capitalisation autour de 2,2 millions de dollars le 12 octobre, après une chute de moitié en vingt-quatre heures, alors qu'elle avait dépassé 4,75 millions le week-end précédent. Le leaker reconnaît avoir vendu à deux reprises, en ne prélevant selon lui que des frais de transaction. Il rejette les accusations d'arnaque, qu'il attribue surtout à des youtubeurs. Le jeton était, répète-t-il, « un don, jamais un investissement ». Ceux qui avaient acheté le jeton dans l'espoir d'obtenir le jeu complet ne l'auront pas.
Avant de partir, CyberLeek a publié une dernière vidéo courte, qu'il présente comme des extraits des ultimes missions et que rien ne permet d'authentifier. Il affirme détenir la fin du jeu, mais dit renoncer à la publier parce qu'elle punirait Take-Two en gâchant l'expérience de joueurs « qui n'ont rien fait de mal ».
Le message se termine sur « The leeks stop here. For now. », soit « les fuites s'arrêtent ici, pour l'instant », avec le jeu de mots sur les poireaux (leeks) d'où vient son pseudonyme. CyberLeek prévient aussi qu'il garde des révélations sur l'histoire en réserve, qu'un mécanisme automatique mettrait en ligne si quelqu'un le faisait taire. La menace vise la traque judiciaire lancée par Take-Two, qui a réclamé des assignations à Discord, Microsoft, X et YouTube pour l'identifier. L'existence de ce dispositif automatique n'est pas établie. Les extraits diffusés en deux mois ne prouvent pas non plus que CyberLeek possède le jeu complet.
Rockstar n'a pas commenté ces dernières images. Le studio vient de retracer la genèse de GTA 6 pour Bloomberg , piratage de 2022 compris, en promettant que son prochain jeu ne demandera pas huit ans de travail.
L'ultimatum de CyberLeek sur le disque visait un vrai point faible, puisque les boîtes de GTA 6 ne contiendront qu'un code de téléchargement, comme le rappelle notre dossier sur la sortie . Il a surtout servi à faire monter le jeton. GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series. D'ici là, toute « version complète » proposée hors des boutiques officielles reste un piège.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leak Saga Comes to Unceremonious End as Cryptocoin Collapses
articles.chapeau: After attempting to use his Cryptocoin to tease leaks, Cyberleek has announced the end of his GTA leaking career.
articles.txt:
By Michael Manning Published Oct 14, 2026, 2:10 PM EDT Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of art has something worth celebrating. He's excited to bring this outlook to Dualshockers. Sign in to your DualShockers account Leaks are an almost unavoidable part of the AAA gaming industry, with the chance of leaks only increasing the bigger the release is. Grand Theft Auto 6 has had an absolute saga of leaks over its development, each put out by a different individual eager to turn the fame of exposing gameplay early into something more.
We mark the end of maybe the most convoluted leak saga in recent years. As reported by Paul Tassi for Forbes , Cyberleek, infamous for releasing nude footage of both GTA 6 protagonists before adding a roadmap to his cryptocoin, suddenly made a post giving up on the venture entirely after fans crashed the coin. A surprise end to a truly baffling series of releases, showing just how quickly 'fame' can backfire.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is easily one of the most anticipated game releases of all time, with fans devouring any chance of extra info they can find no matter the source. After all, Netflix doesn't advertise trailer drops on their service for just anyone, and truly massive development and desire for news has opened a few cracks in Rockstar's pipeline.
We've seen a few of these leakers come and go already, each enjoying their time in the sun before either losing community favor or running out of footage to unveil. Most recently, Cyberleek has been the name to follow, coming on to the scene decrying Take-Two's anti-consumer practices as the motivation for his leaking.
Armed with a fully playable build complete with story missions , Cyberleek didn't open with footage of a mission or a high wanted-level police chase; instead, he opened with both GTA 6 protagonists buck naked, showing off every angle before vanishing as quickly as he came. Soon after, he returned, offering up more footage via a roadmap on his cryptocoin, with new footage drops coinciding with new peaks for the coin itself.
A sudden end to a truly baffling series of releases, showing just how quickly 'fame' can backfire.
This, clearly, made his "pro-consumer" shtick a bit harder to fully believe, even after he released massive text posts denying any kind of greed on his end. In response, players completely tanked the coin, crashing it far below its initial peak when the leaks had begun. Since then, Cyberleek has pulled out of the leaking game, not before declaring he has a 'dead-man's switch' of sorts, primed to release story spoilers for GTA 6 if he's ever caught by Take-Two.
Attempting to cover his tracks from both players' criticisms and Take-Two's legal team, Cyberleek's possession of a seemingly finished copy of GTA 6 is truly baffling. Rockstar has had a terrible time with leaks over the last few months, responding by releasing more footage themselves to totally overpower these leakers to some really impressive effect.
Cyberleek's failed cryptocoin is another chapter in leakers of all kinds attempting to convert their fame from leaking into some kind of following. A few have managed short-term fanbases that follow them for releases, but the constant demand for new drops leaves little love lost when the dust finally settles.
When it comes to leaks, players are ruthless, with very little patience for leakers' antics. Whether they acknowledge it or not, leaking screws over plenty of people, and the players seeking them out have little remorse when the other shoe finally drops. As Grand Theft Auto 6's release rapidly approaches, and Rockstar shows more and more footage themselves, it feels like the saga of leaks might finally be petering out.
Every new, up-and-coming leaker will be met with hesitation after Cyberleek's stunt, giving Rockstar time to swoop in and attract audience attention with their own official drops as the days count down. In the endless rat race of stolen company footage, there really is no love lost between leaker and player, no matter how pro-consumer they try to posture.

articles.txt:
GTA Rockstar assure que ses prochains jeux sortiront plus vite que GTA 6 par Ludovic Quinson Publié : 14 oct. 2026, 11:52 Sauvegarder pour plus tard Sauvegarder pour plus tard Rockstar Games Ajouter comme source préférée sur Google Suivre sur Google News Après huit années de développement et plusieurs reports, GTA 6 s’apprête enfin à voir le jour. Mais cette attente interminable pourrait bien être une exception dans l’histoire de Rockstar Games.
Selon plusieurs responsables du studio, le travail réalisé sur GTA 6 devrait permettre d’accélérer considérablement le développement de leurs futurs projets, grâce notamment aux technologies et aux équipes mises en place ces dernières années.
Dans un entretien accordé à Jason Schreier de Bloomberg , Phil Hooker, responsable du développement chez Rockstar, et Aaron Garbut sont revenus sur les changements apportés au fonctionnement du studio pendant la création de GTA 6.
Et leur constat est plutôt encourageant puisque les années investies dans ce projet ne serviront pas uniquement au prochain Grand Theft Auto. Phil Hooker explique que le moteur graphique, les outils et les équipes constituées pour GTA 6 représentent désormais une base solide sur laquelle Rockstar pourra s’appuyer.
Plutôt que de devoir constamment repousser les limites techniques à chaque nouveau jeu, le studio espère pouvoir réutiliser ces fondations pour se concentrer davantage sur la création de contenu.
Aaron Garbut partage cette vision. Selon lui, le développement de GTA 6 a entraîné des transformations majeures dans les méthodes de travail de Rockstar, et il n’est pas question de tout reconstruire à partir de zéro pour les prochaines productions.
GTA 6 a pris plus de 10 ans à développer mais le prochain jeu Rockstar pourrait sortir plus vite
GTA 6 a raté “plusieurs échéances”, mais une sortie en 2025 est toujours prévue
Take-Two laisse deviner une fenêtre de sortie optimiste pour GTA 6
L’objectif serait donc de réduire le temps nécessaire à la conception des futurs jeux, sans pour autant revoir les ambitions du studio à la baisse.
Il faut dire que GTA 6 représente un chantier particulièrement colossal pour Rockstar Games. Initialement attendu fin 2025, le jeu a d’abord été repoussé au 26 mai 2026 avant que sa sortie soit finalement fixée au 19 novembre 2026.
Avec environ huit années de développement, il s’agit du projet le plus long jamais entrepris par le studio. Strauss Zelnick, PDG de Take-Two Interactive, avait déjà souligné à plusieurs reprises la complexité exceptionnelle du jeu. Rockstar a également reconnu que son univers était devenu si vaste qu’il serait impossible d’en présenter toutes les possibilités uniquement à travers l’histoire principale.
Ces ambitions expliquent en partie pourquoi GTA 6 a nécessité autant de temps et de ressources, mais elles ont également poussé le studio à moderniser une grande partie de ses technologies.
Pour l’instant, Rockstar n’a pas officiellement dévoilé son prochain grand projet, mais plusieurs licences pourraient prendre la relève après GTA 6.
Si les fans espèrent notamment découvrir un jour Red Dead Redemption 3, une autre possibilité a récemment refait surface, il s’agit de L.A. Noire 2. Une ancienne fuite datant de 2023, dont l’auteur aurait correctement anticipé plusieurs détails de GTA 6, affirme que Rockstar préparerait une suite à son jeu d’enquête de 2011.
Ce nouvel épisode se déroulerait à San Francisco, avec une intrigue centrée sur le célèbre tueur du Zodiaque et une sortie envisagée aux alentours de 2030. Rien n’a toutefois été confirmé par Rockstar, et ces informations restent à prendre avec précaution.
À plus court terme, le studio doit également préparer l’avenir de GTA 6, notamment sa version PC, dont la sortie serait envisagée début 2027, ainsi que l’évolution de GTA Online .

articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6 could release on PC in early 2027, according to a new report, shortening the wait after its November console launch.
articles.txt:
By Hannah Hunt Published Oct 14, 2026, 1:47 PM EDT Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider , where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider ’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.
Rockstar fans on PC know the routine by now. A major game arrives on consoles, everyone starts talking about it, and anyone waiting for a computer version has to keep dodging spoilers . Owning hardware capable of running the game doesn’t help much when there’s no version available to install.
That wait can also turn an anticipated release into an expensive decision. Players can buy a console to join in immediately or hold out for their preferred platform without knowing when it will arrive. Grand Theft Auto V made PC players wait roughly nineteen months after its original console debut. A new report suggests Rockstar’s next trip to Vice City could reach them considerably sooner.
Grand Theft Auto VI is reportedly targeting a PC release in the first quarter of 2027 , according to new reports . Four anonymous industry sources familiar with Rockstar’s plans were cited in the report , placing the proposed launch between January and March. With the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S versions scheduled for November 19, 2026, that would reduce the gap to months, although Rockstar has not announced a PC release date.
Four people, four completely different ways of being somebody's family. Here is your seat at the table, what the rest of them would rely on you for, and the thing you would have to watch.
You are the head of the table, and you did not ask for the job so much as end up holding it. Dom is the gravity of this franchise, which is why the films work best when everybody else is circling around whatever he has decided.
You are the one who says the thing out loud and then does not take it back. Letty is the least sentimental person at that table and somehow the most loyal, which is a combination almost nobody manages.
You are the reason anybody remembers the night. Roman talks first, thinks second and is far more frightened than he lets on, which is precisely what makes him the most human person in the whole family.
You are the one who made the plan work while everybody else was busy being heroic about it. Tej does not need the credit, which is fortunate, because in this family the credit tends to go to whoever drove fastest.
Lucia in 'GTA 6' Image via Rockstar Games Jason in 'Grand Theft Auto 6' Image via Rockstar Games The comparison with GTA V explains why this window would matter. That game first released on consoles in September 2013, before reaching PC in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 also launched on consoles first, debuting October 26, 2018, with its PC release following on November 5, 2019. A first-quarter launch for GTA VI would be substantially faster than either. For players considering a console purchase specifically for the sequel, that changes the calculation . Waiting a few months is a different proposition from potentially missing more than a year of conversation around the game. It could make holding onto an existing PC the more appealing option. The report still describes a planned window, however, so it doesn’t give buyers a confirmed alternative to November’s console release.
Rockstar’s announced story follows Jason and Lucia , whose criminal partnership pulls them into a conspiracy across Leonida after an easy score goes wrong. The setting brings the series back to modern-day Vice City, with the surrounding state expanding the adventure beyond the familiar destination. The official launch announcement says the additional development time is intended to deliver the polish players expect .
For now, November 19 remains the confirmed release date for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S , with early 2027 the reported target for PC.

Bloomberg uncovers the details behind how Rockstar created its most ambitious game.
Grand Theft Auto 6: What We Know about Rockstar's Anticipated Game
While the whole world is waiting for GTA 6 to arrive, you can get a glimpse of its long development in Bloomberg's new article , full of curious details and reports.
Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development for over 8 years, and Rockstar took it very seriously, going to Miami to feel Vice City vibes, visiting nightclubs, making helicopter shots, and even riding with police to criminal hotspots.
It wasn't always fun: there was a "dark period", according to development lead Rob Nelson, when the vision wasn't clear. The company grew from 2,441 in its Red Dead Redemption 2 era to 4,711, all to make sure the game would be its most ambitious and most detailed project.
By 2022, GTA 6 looked coherent, after years of struggle. "The pattern is very familiar," said Phil Hooker, one of the three heads of development. "You go through a period where things don’t work, but you see snippets."
The game was delayed twice, and the team felt the delays were necessary. The second time Rockstar’s head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe went to Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick to ask for one, just months after the first, he was baffled:
“I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” she recalled. “But once we talked through why, he got it. And I think we are really lucky that he is as reasonable as he is, because a lot of people would say, ‘You’d just better figure out how to ship it.’ And we have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great.” Zelnick says that generally it’s “a wise investment in time and financial resources” if a game needs to be delayed to “reach the level of perfection it has the ability to reach.”
Apparently, there were no big, dramatic reasons for the delays, but many pieces didn't quite work as expected. For example, the team just didn't have the production capabilities to set up the enormous number of NPCs, reportedly as clever as ever . In response, the company quickly opened a new office and filled it with developers who'd work on the NPCs.
In spite of the delays, Rockstar was making a game to be proud of: “Despite all the concerns and doubts that plague you at that time thinking, ‘If we stick to our guns on this, we have something really special,’” Hooker shared.
Bloomberg's report cautiously says that November 19 seems to be the final release date for GTA 6, but you can never be 100% sure until you're actually playing it.
The good news is the PC version will allegedly be out much, much earlier than anticipated: in 2027 . If you want to know everything we know about the game, check out this article .

Major retailers, including PlayStation Direct , Best Buy , Amazon (including bundle offers), Target , and Walmart , are sold out. With the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI , the reseller market has gotten a little ridiculous (as has everything else).
Beyond the obvious hype for Rockstar's next release, Sony is dealing with broader supply chain bottlenecks. The global AI boom is squeezing the semiconductor market , which means Sony can't build consoles fast enough. According to distributor reports , these supply constraints could keep stock tight well into 2027.
Naturally, scalpers are having a field day. We've seen third-party listings on reseller sites (and even GameStop's official pre-owned page ) gouging buyers for $1,300 to $1,500+ for a console that retails for $899 . Sony is taking the issue so seriously that in Japan, they're forcing buyers to enter a lottery — and prove they've clocked at least 60 hours of PS4 or PS5 playtime over the last two years — just for a chance to buy a PS5 Pro.
If you absolutely have to buy one today and have money to burn, here's what the third-party market currently looks like:
Swappa: This is a legitimate, verified marketplace for used tech. However, verified PS5 Pro listings are currently sitting at $1,338.

Bookmark and refresh product pages. Keep direct product pages saved for PlayStation Direct , Best Buy , Amazon , Target , and Walmart . PlayStation Direct in particular occasionally drops invite-only or queue-based stock.

Preorder the game now. Don't hold your breath for a last-minute GTA 6 PS5 Pro console bundle. Secure your physical or digital preorder now so you're ready to go, no matter which console sits under your TV on day one.

articles.t: We guessed late 2027 for GTA 6 on PC. Industry insiders say Q1 2027
articles.chapeau: Four insiders say that GTA 6 will land on PC in Q1 2027. Rockstar hasn't confirmed, but it would be an unusually short wait.
articles.txt:
We’ve known since February that Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out this year on November 19th, but only for Xbox and PlayStation. In August, Rockstar released an exclusive sneak peek on Netflix with gameplay footage and narrative cutscenes. People are hyped, to say the least.
But what about the PC version? Last month, we ran a quick analysis and estimated a proper PC release for GTA 6 sometime in late 2027 or early 2028. Well, it seems we were off the mark by a tad. According to GamesBeat , the PC version of GTA 6 is slated for release in Q1 2027—much sooner than anyone realistically expected.
GamesBeat gathered the details from four industry insiders who are familiar with Rockstar’s plans and asked to remain anonymous so as not to jeopardize their business relationships. A spokesperson for Rockstar Games did not respond to GamesBeat’s request for comment.
If GTA 6 actually does release a PC version in Q1 2027, that will represent an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases for a Rockstar title. For comparison, GTA 5 released on consoles in September 2013 and followed on PC in April 2015, nearly 18 months later.

articles.t: De nouvelles images pour GTA 6 avec des informations sur les coulisses du développement
articles.chapeau: Rockstar Games et le média Bloomberg dévoilent de nouvelles images de GTA 6 et donnent des détails sur la production du jeu.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games et le média Bloomberg dévoilent de nouvelles images de GTA 6 et donnent des détails sur la production du jeu.
Alors que GTA 6 doit sortir dans 36 jours seulement , la communication s’intensifie autour du prochain jeu de Rockstar. Ce midi, le média Bloomberg a publié un important article autour d’une visite du studio Rockstar North, le principal studio de la firme étoilée.
Au cours de cette visite, fin septembre, Bloomberg a pu s’entretenir avec Jennifer Kolbe, responsable de l’édition chez Rockstar, ainsi que Rob Nelson, Aaron Garbut et Phil Hooker, les trois responsables du développement chez Rockstar North.
Au cours de cette visite, Rockstar Games a confirmé que le développement du jeu (sans la phase de conceptualisation ou de pré-production) à durée huit ans. De fin 2018, à 2026. Le développement est d’ailleurs toujours en cours, mais approche de la fin . Bloomberg affirme que les différentes barres des tâches des différents moniteurs des employés de Rockstar North étaient toutes dans le vert, affirmant que les équipes étaient dans les temps.
Ce sont 12 studios , avec pas moins de 4711 personnes , contre 2441 pour Red Dead Redemption II qui travaillent sur GTA 6 . Depuis 2018, Rockstar Games a donc doublé ses effectifs.
Au début, le projet se nommait, en interne, « Project Americas ». Rockstar comptait, à la base, inclure de vastes territoires couvrant l’Amérique du Nord et l’Amérique du Sud . L’idée de départ était de produire GTA 6 en parallèle de Red Dead Redemption II . Ce plan fut abandonné au fur et à mesure de la production de Red Dead Redemption II qui est devenu bien plus ambitieux que prévu , faisant prendre de nombreuses années de retard à GTA 6 .
Le Covid fut également une épreuve, puisque cette période de télétravail a drastiquement fait baisser la performance du studio et la productivité . De nombreux vétérans et concepteurs expérimentés, frustrés par ce qu’ils percevaient comme une absence de progrès, ont fini par démissionner.
C’est à partir de 2022, avec le lancement de la production active du jeu que les choses ont commencé à prendre forme. Rockstar pouvait enfin visualiser, en gros, à quoi allait ressembler le titre, bien que les grandes lignes de l’histoire et de l’intrigue ont été bouclées à la fin de l’année 2019. C’est à ce moment que le studio a misé sur de nouvelles technologies et systèmes d’IA (l’intelligence artificielle des PNJ en jeu, et non de l’IA comme ChatGPT) pour apporter une réelle immersion en jeu.
L’objectif était de produire une nouvelle IA plus complexe permettant de rendre le monde plus cohérent, et notamment les interactions de Jason et Lucia, afin qu’ils agissent comme un couple , même en dehors des missions. Un pari osé et réussi, puisque des années plus tard, cela représente un des aspects fondamentaux du jeu :
Dans la peau de Jason, le joueur peut envoyer un SMS à Lucia pour lui proposer de se voir. Quelques minutes plus tard, ils se promènent dans un parc, main dans la main, en évoquant le souvenir de la fois où la mère de Lucia s’était fâchée contre lui. Ils peuvent ensuite aller à la salle de sport (Lucia monte peut-être sur le tapis de course pendant que Jason enchaîne les squats) ou braquer un magasin ensemble tout en étant poursuivis par la police, le tout ponctué de flirt et de taquineries. Observer l’interaction entre les deux personnages ajoutait une dimension inédite aux systèmes d’immersion hérités des précédents titres de Rockstar.
Rockstar Games a voulu reproduire l’ambiance, les couleurs et l’âme de la Floride, dans le but de créer une authenticité maximale de la ville de Miami. L’objectif est de faire de GTA 6 un jeu extrêmement immersif, où les joueurs se laissent portés et vont se perdre dans le monde de Leonida. Phil Hooker a fait part d’une expérience qu’il a pu vivre quelques semaines avant la visite de Bloomberg. Un moment dans le jeu qui lui a procuré une grande joie.
Vers la fin du développement de GTA VI, Hooker testait une version du jeu ; alors qu’il se dirigeait vers une mission du scénario, il heurta une autre voiture dont le conducteur riposta en le percutant en retour tout en lui criant dessus. articles.t: GTA 6 Lead Reacts To The Infamous 2022 Leak: 'Like Somebody's Wading Through Your Dirty Washing'
articles.chapeau: Rockstar also said it likely won't return to a work-from-home model as too many people want to 'steal' its games
articles.txt:
In 2022, Grand Theft Auto 6 suffered a massive, unprecedented leak, giving players a very early look at the still-in-development open-world sequel. Four years later, and just a few weeks before GTA 6′ s release on November 19, Rockstar North’s head of development and co-studio head Aaron Garbut explained how it felt to see the leak spread online.
On October 14, Bloomberg published an in-depth and lengthy report about Rockstar’s work on GTA 6 and how it has expanded to become one of the biggest game developers in the world. And in the report, Garbut talked openly about seeing unfinished clips of GTA 6 circulating all across the internet and described how it felt in the moment.
“It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” said Garbut. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that.”
The longtime Rockstar vet who has worked on the GTA franchise since the very first game also said that it felt “weirdly invasive” to see those clips online, adding that it was “quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
Following the 2022 leak, Rockstar Games started reversing some of its work-from-home policies and practices, and in 2024 all employees had to be back in the office five days a week. The company cited security concerns for the return-to-office policy. Rockstar also banned all devs from accessing the company’s servers and tools from home, forcing them to use vacation or sick days if they needed to stay home for childcare or other emergencies. Rockstar Games plans to reexamine its policies after GTA 6 ships, but head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe doubted the studio would move back to a hybrid model any time soon.
“The idea that we would have the game in that many environments is something that I think the security team would not love,” explained Kolbe.
“I think if we did not have a game that people wanted to steal as much, maybe it would be an easier conversation.”
Despite these restrictions, in August, Cyberleek began sharing Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay leaks online. Bloomberg reports this led to frustration at the studio, as devs felt they had sacrificed much and it didn’t matter in the end, as leaks still happened. On Wednesday, Cyberleek claimed to be done leaking GTA 6 clips.

articles.t: GTA 6 : le hacker Cyberleek met fin aux fuites et renonce à publier le jeu complet
articles.chapeau: Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l'arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu'il affirme détenir.
articles.txt:
Sony détaille un peu plus la rétrocompatibilité sur sa PlayStation 5. Il sera possible de jouer à la grande majorité des jeux PlayStation 4 sur la PS5, mais tous ne seront pas compatibles.
Le leaker Cyberleek annonce l’arrêt de ses fuites de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) et renonce à publier la version complète du jeu qu’il affirme détenir . Dans un message publié aujourd’hui sur son site, le hacker explique que son objectif financier n’a pas été atteint, tout en laissant planer la possibilité de nouvelles révélations.
Dans un message en trois parties intitulé The End of the Road , Cyberleek confirme qu’il ne publiera pas la version jouable complète de GTA 6 qu’il prétend avoir en sa possession. Le hacker affirmait auparavant pouvoir diffuser l’intégralité du mode histoire, jusqu’au générique de fin, si sa cryptomonnaie atteignait 30 millions de dollars. Cet objectif n’ayant pas été atteint, la publication est annulée.
Cyberleek avance également un argument pratique : mettre en ligne anonymement un fichier de plus de 200 Go présenterait des risques importants, sans contrepartie financière suffisante. L’existence de cette version complète et sa taille restent toutefois non vérifiées. Aucun élément indépendant ne permet de confirmer que le pirate possède réellement une copie jouable intégrale du prochain jeu de Rockstar Games.
L’annonce intervient après plusieurs semaines de leaks d’extraits de gameplay issus d’une version de développement . Le leaker avait notamment publié une longue séquence montrant Jason et Lucia, les deux protagonistes, ainsi que différentes situations de jeu. Certaines images semblaient provenir de missions avancées de l’histoire.
Cyberleek affirme également connaître le dénouement du jeu, mais assure avoir choisi de ne pas le révéler afin de préserver l’expérience des joueurs. Il soutient que les dernières séquences publiées proviennent de missions finales, présentées sans leur contexte narratif pour éviter de dévoiler les principaux rebondissements.
Le message contient toutefois une réserve importante : « Les fuites s’arrêtent ici. Pour l’instant »/ Cyberleek affirme aussi avoir activé un mécanisme de publication différée qui déclencherait la diffusion de spoilers s’il était pris pour cible par les autorités. Cette menace entretient donc l’incertitude sur la suite de l’affaire, malgré l’annonce d’un arrêt des publications de leaks.
La campagne de Cyberleek associait les révélations sur GTA 6 à une cryptomonnaie portant son nom. En échange d’une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars, le leaker promettait de publier le jeu complet. Il avait également posé une autre condition à Take-Two, maison mère de Rockstar Games : sortir le jeu sur disque physique et présenter des excuses publiques. Pour rappel, Grand Theft Auto VI sera uniquement disponible en version numérique . Cyberleek rejette les accusations selon lesquelles cette opération aurait constitué une escroquerie destinée à faire monter artificiellement la valeur du token avant sa revente.
Rockstar Games n’a pas publiquement commenté cette dernière annonce. Sa maison mère, Take-Two, cherche néanmoins à identifier le ou les responsables des fuites, notamment au moyen de procédures judiciaires visant à obtenir des informations auprès de plateformes en ligne. Discord et Microsoft ont partie des plateformes visées . La publication du jeu complet n’est donc plus à l’ordre du jour selon Cyberleek, mais rien ne garantit que les fuites cesseront définitivement avant la sortie officielle de GTA 6 , prévue le 19 novembre sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X/S.
Merci de nous avoir signalé l'erreur, nous allons corriger cela rapidement.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' file size: Cyberleek reveals eye-watering storage requirements
articles.chapeau: Take it with a grain of salt, of course.
articles.txt:
The person leaking a bunch of gameplay videos of Grand Theft Auto VI may have just revealed the most useful information in all of their leaks.
On the Cyberleek website (per our colleagues at PCMag ), one of the latest updates included a threat to release a full build of the game in some form if people on the internet raised the leaker's crypto memecoin to a $30 million market cap. The coin has since crashed and looks like it's not going to get anywhere close to that level, but more importantly, the update included a file size for the playable build they have evidently been taking clips from: 200GB.
That's obviously a huge number, and makes up more than 20 percent of the usable storage space on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X console. Perhaps surprisingly, it's not as big as some other games, as recent Call of Duty titles clear 200GB by a good margin. But it would still be one of the biggest single-player file sizes we've seen yet, and speaks to the scale and scope of GTA 6 .
Of course, this should be taken with at least a tiny bit of skepticism. We don't know much about the build Cyberleek has been leaking footage from. If they do indeed have the full game on hand, it could be an older build that hasn't been fully optimized yet, so the true GTA 6 file size could theoretically be smaller once the actual game comes out on Nov. 19.

articles.txt:
Si tous les regards étaient braqués sur CyberLeek cet été, les choses ont bien changé depuis que Rockstar dévoile des images de GTA 6 presque tous les jours. Même si les fuites causent encore beaucoup de soucis à Rockstar et Take-Two, culturellement parlant, elles n’ont presque plus aucun impact et deviennent assez ignorées. De quoi mettre en péril le pari boursier que CyberLeek tentait autour de ces fuites, c’est pourquoi le groupe a décidé d’arrêter les frais.
La fin d’un feuilleton dangereux Il ne voudra pas l’avouer dans ces termes, mais l’arnaque économique que CyberLeek mettait en place autour des fuites de GTA 6 tombe à l’eau. Plus tôt dans la semaine, il déclarait vouloir que sa propre cryptomonnaie atteigne les 30 millions de dollars de capitalisation boursière, alors qu’il peinait à dépasser les 5 millions ces derniers jours. S’il atteignait cet objectif, il disait vouloir sortir le jeu complet dans la nature . L’annonce a eu l’effet souhaité inverse, c’est-à-dire que durant les jours suivants, le cours a considérablement baissé.
Conscient qu’il ne pouvait plus tirer grand-chose des fuites, CyberLeek a donc décidé de mettre fin à son aventure. Il affirme qu’il a réfléchi à l’idée de poster la fin du jeu sur les réseaux sociaux, mais estime que Take-Two et Rockstar ont déjà retenu la leçon et que cela ne ferait qu’impacter le public (relayé par Insider Gaming ) :
« CL (CYBERLEEKS) détient la fin [de GTA 6]. L’idée a été envisagée. Cela aurait puni considérablement Take-Two, mais ça aurait gâché l’expérience des joueurs, qui n’y étaient pour rien. Take-Two n’aurait fait preuve d’aucune clémence envers CL – pourquoi CL en ferait-il preuve ? Take-Two a déjà été suffisamment puni. La fin ne sera pas publiée. »
Derrière cette posture, c’est surtout le signe que les fuites n’intéressent plus autant qu’avant et que le risque de se faire attraper reste grand. Cela n’en vaut donc plus la peine, et on peut désormais refermer ce chapitre en attendant la sortie du jeu, prévue pour le 19 novembre.

articles.chapeau: Treize ans après GTA 5, Rockstar fixe enfin la sortie de GTA 6 et s’explique sur son cycle démesuré. Le studio promet aussi une date de sortie GTA 7 bien plus proche, mais à quelles conditions ?
articles.txt:
Treize ans après GTA 5, Rockstar fixe enfin la sortie de GTA 6 et s’explique sur son cycle démesuré. Le studio promet aussi une date de sortie GTA 7 bien plus proche, mais à quelles conditions ?
Treize ans. C’est le temps qui se sera écoulé entre la sortie de GTA 5 en 2013 et celle de GTA 6 , désormais fixée au 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Un cycle gigantesque qui a nourri blagues et inquiétudes chez les joueurs : faudra-t-il attendre les années 2040 pour poser les mains sur GTA 7 ?
La réponse est plus nuancée. Dans une interview accordée à Bloomberg, rapportée par GamesRadar, le directeur technique de Rockstar Games , Phil Hooker , assure que les prochains projets, y compris un hypothétique Grand Theft Auto VII , devraient arriver bien plus vite grâce au nouveau moteur, aux outils et à l’équipe mis en place pour GTA 6 .
Officiellement, le développement de GTA 6 a commencé en 2015, puis l’équipe a vraiment accéléré après la sortie de Red Dead Redemption 2 en 2018. Avec une sortie désormais visée en 2026, on parle d’environ onze ans de chantier et de treize ans d’écart avec GTA 5 . Ce temps s’explique par l’ampleur du projet : le nouvel État de Leonida et sa Vice City moderne seraient nettement plus vastes et denses que Los Santos, avec bien plus de zones urbaines, d’intérieurs, d’animations et de comportements d’intelligence artificielle à produire.
C’est en coulisses que se joue pourtant la vraie différence pour GTA 7 . Rockstar Games a passé des années à refondre son moteur maison RAGE et ses outils internes. Phil Hooker résume auprès de Bloomberg : « Le moteur, les outils et l’équipe que nous avons bâtis pendant ce projet vont nous permettre de faire les choses plus vite. » Il se dit confiant pour « construire davantage en largeur qu’en hauteur ». Son collègue Aaron Garbut insiste : « Nous avons changé énormément de choses de fond sur ce projet, mais maintenant c’est fait et nous n’allons pas tout démonter. »
Concrètement, cela ne signifie pas que la date de sortie de GTA 7 se rapprochera des cycles de trois ou quatre ans d’autres licences. Le studio n’a rien annoncé officiellement, et plusieurs analystes situent plutôt une fenêtre réaliste au début des années 2030, entre 2032 et 2035, en tenant compte du support long de GTA 6 (mode en ligne, version PC, extensions). Les propos de Phil Hooker et Aaron Garbut laissent surtout penser que Rockstar Games pourra éviter de refaire une refonte technique complète à chaque épisode. Résultat probable : un écart réduit sous les treize ans, peut être autour de huit à dix ans, mais aucune rumeur ne peut aujourd’hui prétendre connaître le vrai calendrier.

articles.txt:
(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter GTA 6 has suffered its fair share of leaks now, with 25 minutes of new gameplay having gone live last week – and it hasn't been easy for Rockstar Games , to say the least.
Artist Aaron Garbut tells Bloomberg as much during a recent interview, describing leaks as a line crossed – a look into something personal, and unprepared for the public. "It feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing," he says. "It's like they're inside your head." That makes sense, honestly… and that first major GTA 6 leak in 2022 was when this awful feeling really started to hit the developers.
"You see your early work out there," Garbut describes. "Nobody's ever supposed to see that. It's really weirdly invasive. And so it's quite hard to deal with on an emotional level." I can only imagine myself – and it certainly doesn't help that the leaks haven't slowed down at all, really, despite Rockstar taking legal action against folks responsible for them in the past. The cryptocurrency-fueled GTA 6 leak (leaks, more like) from "Cyberleek" comes to mind.
That whole debacle was supposedly spurred by demands for digital rights , more physical copies, and such, with claims to be "raising funds for a secret project" (via crypto, of course) – but it's now apparently dead after the leaker behind it saw their meme coin crash and fall some $20 million short of their market cap goal. They set the goal as a precursor to leaking the entirety of GTA 6, supposedly… even though the full game is, uh, out next month.
So, will we see any more GTA 6 leaks come to light? I'd wager we won't, considering the November 19 release date and all, but who knows – Rockstar's cookin' up one heck of a massive game, and there's bound to be quite a lot that we've not seen out of it yet. I'm not sure it would count as "dirty washing" at this point, either, seeing as it's so, so close to launch. I'd say it likely qualifies as clean and then some.
GTA 6 took 13 years, but GTA 7 won't – Rockstar says "the tools and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly" in the future

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker Suddenly Quits After Crypto Flop, but Something Doesn't Add Up
articles.chapeau: Cyberleek has abandoned its threatened GTA 6 release after failing to hit a $30 million cryptocurrency target. But was the complete game ever in its possession?
articles.txt:
Facebook X Pinterest Cyberleek has backed down from its alleged GTA 6 full-game leak after a failed cryptocurrency campaign. Image credit: Rockstar Games. Cyberleek spent days threatening to release a complete, playable copy of GTA 6 if its cryptocurrency reached a $30 million market capitalization. Now, the anonymous leaker has abruptly abandoned the plan after failing to hit that target, claiming that uploading the alleged 200GB game build would be too risky. It’s a convenient explanation, although it raises questions about whether Cyberleek ever possessed the complete game in the first place.
The announcement came on October 14, alongside another GTA 6 gameplay video and a warning about potential story spoilers. Cyberleek also claims to possess the game’s ending but says it has decided against revealing it.
In a three-part farewell statement titled “The End of the Road”, Cyberleek confirmed that its cryptocurrency failed to reach the $30 million target.
“The 30M was not reached, so no build,” the leaker stated, arguing that anonymously distributing more than 200GB of game files carried too much risk without the financial incentive.
Just days earlier, Cyberleek had threatened to release GTA 6’s complete single-player campaign , including its ending, unless the cryptocurrency reached its target or Take-Two met a series of demands.
What’s questionable is that those risks existed long before the cryptocurrency campaign failed. Cyberleek knew what it was threatening to do, yet suddenly decided the release wasn’t worth pursuing once the financial target fell short.
Of course, the leaker never guaranteed an unconditional release. But the abrupt reversal still leaves the alleged complete build unverified.
See also : GTA 6 PC Release Date Could Break Rockstar’s Long-Standing PC Launch Pattern
Despite announcing its departure, Cyberleek reportedly published another four-minute gameplay video featuring Lucia visiting a hair salon, robbing a store, playing pool, and trying on clothes. The footage also includes a cinematic sequence that the leaker claims comes from the game’s final missions.
That claim hasn’t been independently verified, and we won’t discuss the alleged ending footage to avoid spoilers.
Cyberleek also claims to have established a dead man’s switch that would release story spoilers if the group were targeted. Whether such a mechanism exists is unknown.
There’s another problem with the promised 200GB build. Cyberleek never clearly established whether it was intended for PC, PS5, or Xbox. Even if genuine, a leaked development build might require specialized hardware or software, potentially leaving ordinary gamers unable to play it.
Releasing game files and releasing something people can actually play are two very different things.

The timing of Cyberleek’s departure is difficult to ignore. The group used the possibility of a full GTA 6 release to promote a speculative cryptocurrency, then abandoned that promise when the token failed to reach its target.
Cyberleek has denied accusations of a rug pull and claims the cryptocurrency was always intended as a donation rather than an investment. However, these explanations don’t establish whether the promised game build ever existed.
Cyberleek may genuinely have access to unreleased GTA 6 material. Its gameplay footage suggests some level of access to a working version of the game, but that doesn’t prove possession of the complete campaign.
For all the publicity surrounding the leaks, Cyberleek’s biggest claim remains unverified. Gamers were promised the possibility of a playable GTA 6 build, only to receive another gameplay video and a farewell announcement after the cryptocurrency campaign fell short.
Grand Theft Auto VI is still scheduled for November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.t: Cyberleek threatens to ruin end of GTA 6 if Rockstar set their lawyers on them
articles.chapeau: More GTA 6 footage has appeared from Cyberleek, but after failing to hit a $30 million crypto goal, it might be their final video.
articles.txt:
More GTA 6 footage has appeared from Cyberleek, but after failing to hit a $30 million crypto goal, it might be their final video.
GTA 6 has been subject to various leaks over the past few years, but the most invasive and damaging has been caused by the individual or group known as Cyberleek.
The leaker began posting clips in August , in what they claimed was a protest against the lack of physical disc version for GTA 6. However, they’ve been benefitting from crypto donations at the same time, and appeared to run off with around £200,000 a couple of months ago.
After disappearing into the ether, Cyberleek returned earlier this month with nude clips and another crypto incentive – promising they’ll release the full build of GTA 6, supposedly over 200GB in size , if the memecoin hit a $30 million (£22.8 million) market cap.
It turns out, people aren’t that interested in laying down donations to see a game that comes out in just over a month. After failing to hit the milestone, Cyberleek posted an update on their website (which has since been taken down), stating that the build will not be released.
However, they did release another video, the 20th in total, which they claim shows a clip from ‘the final missions’ but ‘out of context’ so they don’t spoil anything.

For obvious reasons we won’t share the clip here, but it initially shows Lucia visiting a barbershop, playing pool in a bar, and trying on outfits in a basketball shop to the song Don’t Stop Believin’ by Journey.
Cyberleek announces the end of GTA 6 leaks after posting the 20th clip, but says the dead man’s switch is active and story spoilers including the ending will be published if Take-Two catches him: “CL has the ending. It was considered. It would punish Take-Two greatly – but ruin… pic.twitter.com/MxsLT460WY
It then suddenly cuts to various transition shots over the game’s city landscape, which is presumably the sequence from the final mission. However, it’s so abstract, it could be pulled from any anywhere.
Cyberleek claims they do have the ending of GTA 6 in their possession, with story spoilers, but they won’t release it unless Take-Two or Rockstar decides to take action against them. ‘The dead man’s switch is active – story spoilers only,’ the post reads. ‘Left alone, it never fires. Whoever removes CL [Cyberleek] chooses it.’
It’s not clear if Cyberleek has thought about what will happen once GTA 6 does launch, making his threat redundant. However, Rockstar probably won’t want a playable build out there for free on the internet at any point, even if it is an early version.
It feels inevitable that Rockstar will catch up with them though, and that they won’t be let off lightly, which makes this whole endeavour thoroughly idiotic in the grand scheme.
Cyberleek concludes their statement with the promise that the ‘leeks stop here’, albeit ‘for now’, presumably in reference to if Rockstar makes moves against them or not. Hopefully though, this will be the actual end this time.
At the very least, we only have just over a month until GTA 6 leaks of any kind become obsolete, with the game set to launch across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X on November 19, 2026.

articles.t: Après Huit Ans De Chantier, GTA 6 Doit Permettre à Rockstar D’avancer Bien Plus Vite
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 aura nécessité environ 8 ans de développement, mais son moteur et ses outils doivent raccourcir la production des prochains jeux Rockstar.
articles.txt:
Huit années de développement auront permis à Rockstar de revoir une large part de ses fondations techniques. Cet investissement massif autour de GTA 6 doit désormais éviter au studio de repartir de zéro pour ses prochains jeux.
Dans une enquête de Bloomberg consacrée aux coulisses du projet, les responsables du développement Phil Hooker et Aaron Garbut expliquent que le moteur, les outils et les équipes constitués pendant ce long chantier permettront à Rockstar d’avancer plus rapidement à l’avenir.
Phil Hooker estime que le studio peut désormais capitaliser sur ce travail plutôt que de reconstruire son environnement de production à chaque projet. Aaron Garbut précise que de nombreux éléments fondamentaux ont été modifiés pour GTA 6, mais que cette base est maintenant achevée et ne sera pas de nouveau démantelée.
Les deux responsables citent GTA 3 et Vice City comme référence. Vice City était sorti environ un an après GTA 3, précisément parce qu’il réutilisait une base technique et créative déjà opérationnelle.
La situation actuelle reste très différente. GTA 6 aura traversé environ huit ans de développement complet, tandis que 13 années séparent sa sortie de celle de GTA 5. Rockstar compte par ailleurs désormais plus de 4 700 employés répartis dans 12 bureaux .
GTA 6 doit arriver le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Le jeu avait d’abord été repoussé à mai 2026, avant qu’un second report ne décale son lancement au mois de novembre.
Le calendrier mouvementé de GTA 6 reste à surveiller, après le troisième report de GTA VI en novembre 2026 .
Rockstar n’a encore dévoilé aucun projet appelé à lui succéder, et ni Phil Hooker ni Aaron Garbut ne donnent de calendrier. Le prochain cycle devrait néanmoins être plus court, sans nécessairement renouer avec la cadence de l’époque Vice City : la taille des mondes ouverts modernes, leur niveau de détail et leur exploitation sur plusieurs années imposent désormais une production autrement plus lourde.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' Cyberleek release updates: What leaked, what's next
articles.chapeau: Maybe don't watch these videos on your work device.
articles.txt:
If you simply can't get enough of Grand Theft Auto VI prior to its Nov. 19 release, there are still new GTA 6 leaks coming out.
Cyberleek , the anonymous entity that has been leaking clips from a pre-release build of GTA 6 since August, made their grand return in October after about a month of silence. Last week, Cyberleek posted a 24-minute video that seemed to show some story sequences and a glimpse of the male protagonist Jason rendered completely nude. That wasn't the end of it.
And, as Cyberleek said they would, nude clips of the female protagonist Lucia soon followed. On top of that, Cyberleek is now threatening to release a development build of the game, and according to Dextero, may have already done so . Websites affiliated with Cyberleek include a link to a file named GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1, locked behind a $40 paywall.
It should go without saying that downloading files from a sketchy website is not a wise idea, nor is purchasing illegal content that violates Rockstar's copyright.
Cyberleek returned this week with more clips that you definitely should not watch at work.
That's because these new clips all center on the female protagonist, Lucia, nude. In the clips, Lucia does mundane things like walk around Vice City, drive a vehicle, and parachute off a skyscraper while wearing little to no clothes (OK, so not entirely mundane, actually). It doesn't seem like anything new has been posted since Monday morning, though.
One thing to note about these clips: The nudity doesn't appear to be a normal element of the gameplay, but rather some type of mod. Rockstar has designed its last couple of big open-world adventures around extremely reactive NPCs, and none of them react at all to seeing Jason or Lucia nude in these leaked clips. Between that, and another clip from last week where the player spawns a tank out of thin air, it sure seems like developer tools are being used to achieve outcomes that will not be possible in the final game.
In other words, don't expect to be able to streak around Vice City in the nude on Nov. 19.
On websites associated with Cyberleek, the leaker threatened to release a full playthrough of the entire GTA 6 story if their memecoin reached $30 million in market value. The leaker also threatened to release a development build of the game if Rockstar failed to meet their demands to release GTA 6 on a physical disc. There's just one problem: The coin is tanking.
IGN reported a market cap of just $1.7 million, well below any of the stretch goals specified by Cyberleek, and certainly not even close to the $7.8 million high it reached on Oct. 11. Despite this, Cyberleek may have made good on their threat to release a development build of the game.
Dextero is reporting that the development build has been posted online, locked behind a $40 paywall. In addition, a Cyberleek website with all of the leaked clips now includes this update, posted on Oct. 13: " DEVELOPMENT BUILD IS OUT: GTA 6: Development Build v1.0.1.08022025 is up. The deal was 30 million marketcap and the build goes out. Cap was not hit. Build is out anyway. $40 per download. Pay it, then take the mirror."
Because the leaker is anonymous, and because it would be illegal and dangerous to download mystery files from an unverified website, we can't confirm that this development build is real, or that it was even directly posted by Cyberleek.
However, if there is now a development build floating around the web, expect to see far more GTA 6 leaks in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 19 release date.
Alternatively, you could wait and play the game when it actually comes out. You can preorder the game now .
A Cyberleek website includes a poll about what type of Lucia content to release next. The poll is set to end on Oct. 14, with the leading option as "Race track."
It seems extremely likely that more clips featuring Lucia are set to be released any day now.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker's Latest Effort Appears To Flop As Group's Meme Coin Declines
articles.chapeau: The GTA 6 leaker, CyberLeek, seems to be frustrated that the group's meme coin has cratered amid scam accusations, prompting it to hit pause.
articles.txt:
The notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker seems to be hitting pause after the group’s newest effort to rake in funds appears to have flopped.
Back on Monday, the culprit, CyberLeek, dangled the prospect of releasing a “Full 200+GB playable build” for GTA 6, ahead of the game’s official release next month. The only catch? CyberLeek said it would only leak the playable build if the group’s cryptocurrency-related meme coin crossed over $30 million in market cap.
Two days later, CyberLeek appears to be backtracking on the offer, according to a new post on the group’s website titled “End of the Road.” In the post, CyberLeek complains about the group’s meme coin falling flat amid accusations that it’s trying to orchestrate a “rugpull,” and cash out on the group’s meme coin once it crosses a certain value.
“The 30M ($30 million) was not reached, so no build. Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk —worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project. Terms honored as written,” the group wrote. “Sad, the negativity —and how few believe anything real is behind this.”
From the get-go, CyberLeek’s activities have faced crypto-scam accusations. That’s because the group’s initial GTA 6 leaks also focused on driving attention to the CyberLeek meme coin, which briefly hit a $23 million total market cap back on August 23rd. But there were signs that CyberLeek cashed out on the meme coin soon after, raking in an estimated $270,000, according to IGN.
The group then went dormant only to return last week with a 25-minute GTA 6 clip all the while asking for more “donations” through the group’s meme coin. CyberLeek then escalated by teasing the leak of an alleged playable build. The gang also threatened GTA 6’s publisher, Take-Two Interactive, writing: “Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks (for the game) and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing.”
But the efforts have so far failed to increase the value of the group’s meme coin. In fact, it’s fallen in value over the last few hours, with the market cap now estimated at a mere $1.24 million.
In response, CyberLeek’s newest post alludes to how some YouTubers and influencers were calling the group’s activities a scam. “The token was always a donation, never an investment,” CyberLeek wrote. “No returns promised, none implied. Rugpull talk comes from people who never opened the chain. Mostly YouTubers. Do not trust them. They have no idea what they are talking about.”
CyberLeek also reasserts it has a playable copy of the game, but refuses to show GTA 6’s ending. “It would punish Take-Two greatly —but ruin the experience for the gamers, who did nothing wrong. Take-Two would show CL no mercy —why should CL show any to them? Still: Take-Two was punished enough. The ending stays unpublished,” the post says.
Although CyberLeek did leak some new footage on Wednesday, supposedly showing some final missions in the game, the group's post adds: “The Edict stands. The leeks stop here. For now.”
So far, Take-Two Interactive hasn’t responded to a request for comment, although the company has been subpoenaing records to identify and catch CyberLeek. In the meantime, some fans have been celebrating the meme coin’s plummeting value all the while bashing the leaks. “He (CyberLeek) tried to boost his coin’s value, failed miserably and is basically throwing a hissy fit that people didn't buy into his coin so that he could get rich off of it. Now that he realizes the well is dry he's running away to hide again,” wrote one user on Reddit.
The other issue is that Take-Two might release an official PC build for GTA 6 as soon as Q1. But for now, the game is launching first on PlayStation and Xbox on November 19th, with preorders already available.

articles.t: New GTA 6 Cyberleek video has story clips and one NSFW detail
articles.chapeau: We're not joking about the NSFW part.
articles.txt:
We thought we were done with notorious Grand Theft Auto VI leaker known only as Cyberleek , but we were proven wrong on Thursday with a fresh GTA 6 leak.
The still-anonymous leaker (or group of leakers) posted their first update since late August, in the form of a nearly 25-minute-long video that's easy enough to find on social media. It's our most detailed look yet at the hotly anticipated game from Rockstar, at least outside of the official "Extended Look" that aired on Netflix in August.
If you manage to find the video, be warned: Major portions of it are strictly not safe for work. It includes a lot of footage of Jason, the male protagonist, walking around completely nude, and everything is modeled in full detail. It's unclear if this is something you can actually do in the final game, or if Cyberleek used some kind of developer tools to pull it off. There are a couple of bits of evidence pointing to the latter; NPCs do not react at all to Jason's nudity, and at one point, the person playing the leaked build spawns a tank out of thin air, suggesting capabilities beyond what normal players will be able to do.
There is also a very brief clip of Lucia, the game's other protagonist, who is seen mostly nude at the very end of the video. There was some speculation earlier in the week that nudity would be part of the game, and it seems like it's at least partially confirmed now.
Beyond the NSFW bits, nothing in the video is all that surprising. We see a couple of different vehicular races, both of which are pre-empted by cutscenes introducing the characters in charge of racing in the countryside and on city streets. These cutscenes aren't especially spoiler-heavy, but if you're really precious about not seeing them ahead of release, you should probably avoid Cyberleek's latest GTA 6 leaks.
We also get a brief look at vehicle customization, which includes the ability to upgrade the engine, transmission, and other aspects of cars. There's also some footage of the game being played in first-person, both while driving and walking around. This was a popular feature Rockstar added to GTA 5 years after release (and incorporated into Red Dead Redemption II ), but it hasn't been shown in GTA 6 yet.

articles.t: Report indicates 'GTA 6' launching on PC in early 2027
articles.chapeau: That's sooner than expected.
articles.txt:
Lots of people are excited about Grand Theft Auto VI , but PC players haven't been sure when they will be able to play it . That might have just changed.
Citing four different industry sources, GamesBeat reported that Rockstar plans to launch GTA 6 on PC in the first quarter of 2027, or by the end of March, in other words. That would certainly be a pivot from the company's previous PC strategy, as GTA 5 came out on PC nearly two years after its console launch, while Red Dead Redemption 2 took a little more than a year to escape consoles.
This is big for a few reasons. First and foremost, if the report is accurate, people who primarily game on PC won't have to wait as long to play GTA 6 as they thought they might have to. It also means anyone who wants the most premium experience possible with the game might not have to agonize over whether or not to buy a PS5 Pro , as PC could offer the best version of the game — if you have a strong enough machine, anyway.
Beyond that, if Rockstar ends up doing an online mode for GTA 6 , the PC version could be the home of the popular and growing GTA roleplaying community, as it has been for GTA 5 . The PC ecosystem allows for much more freedom in terms of supporting user-created content, making it ideal for roleplayers.
